section_summary: This section contains shipping directives and a 1948 despatch on returning responsibility for Japanese merchant vessels to private owners while retaining occupation controls over vessel assignments and sailings. Its enclosures include a SCAP press release, a detailed 1947 study of phased decontrol, a shipowners’ statement, and the opening pages of the Mariners Law. The first page continues an earlier press digest with brief items on Japan, China, and Brazil.

subfiles.title: Press digest: Sino-Japanese amity, shark’s fin, shrine lands, and Japanese activity in Brazil
subfiles.about: Four brief translated news items cover Japanese and Chinese affairs and alleged Japanese terrorist activity in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Continued page of a press digest containing four short news items.

subfiles.title: Identification and Operation of Japanese Merchant Vessels
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards naval instructions on SCAJAP vessel identification and authorized sailing.
subfiles.summary: Describes requirements for SCAJAP numbers and Certificates of Operation and permission for voyages within Japanese home waters.

subfiles.title: Operation of Vessels under the Supervision of the Administrator, SCAJAP
subfiles.about: Sets authorization rules for Japanese vessels sailing inside and outside home waters.
subfiles.summary: Requires authorization for voyages beyond territorial waters and permits domestic and specified fishing voyages without individual approval.

subfiles.title: Suppression of Illegal Entry into Japan, SCAPIN 1393
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Clarifies which authorities may issue permits for voyages beyond Japanese territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: States that SCAJAP authorization is required and addresses purported Allied permits and Korean foreign trade vessels.

subfiles.title: Governmental and Administrative Separation of Certain Outlying Areas from Japan, SCAPIN 677
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Defines areas within and outside Japan for occupation administration.
subfiles.summary: Orders Japan to cease authority over specified outlying territories and defines the geographic scope of future directives.

subfiles.title: Amendment on the Izu and Nanpō Islands, SCAPIN 841
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Amends SCAPIN 677 to include specified islands within its definition of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Restores Japanese administrative jurisdiction over the Izu Islands and northern Nanpō Islands, subject to SCAP authority.

subfiles.title: Area Authorized for Japanese Fishing and Whaling, SCAPIN 1033
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets the authorized geographic area and exclusions for Japanese fishing and whaling.
subfiles.summary: Defines a fishing boundary and limits approaches to certain islands while reserving questions of sovereignty and fishing rights.

subfiles.title: Japanese Vessels: Assignment of SCAJAP Numbers and Issuance of Certificates of Operation
subfiles.about: Requires qualifying Japanese steel vessels to display SCAJAP numbers and carry operating certificates.
subfiles.summary: Specifies covered vessels, application procedures, number markings, and certificate posting.

subfiles.title: Resumption of Responsibility by Japanese Shipowners to Crew, Supply, Repair and Maintain Privately-Owned Merchant Vessels
subfiles.from: T. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the shift from government bareboat chartering to private owners’ operational responsibility under time charters.
subfiles.summary: Sebald explains that owners will again crew, supply, repair, and maintain vessels while SCAJAP retains assignment and sailing control. He reviews the financial weakness of shipping firms, subsidies, surplus labor, maritime law, and the earlier staff study. He endorses the change but judges it overdue.

subfiles.title: SCAP Authorized Limited Private Operation of Japanese Shipping
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces limited return of merchant vessel operations to Japanese private owners.
subfiles.summary: Explains the new time charter arrangement, continuing occupation control over vessel use, treatment of special service vessels, and the depleted size of Japan’s fleet.

subfiles.title: Japanese Merchant Shipping, SCAPIN 1931
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs revised operational responsibilities for government, private, fishing, and merchant vessels.
subfiles.summary: Allocates operation of special service vessels to public agencies or private owners and places other qualifying steel vessels on time charter to the Civilian Merchant Marine Committee. SCAJAP retains administrative control.

subfiles.title: Return of Japanese Merchant Marine to Private Operation by Phased Decontrol from Government Operation
subfiles.from: Paul E. Richers, Civil Transportation Section
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Proposes a staged transfer of Japanese merchant shipping from government operation to private enterprise.
subfiles.summary: The study finds government bareboat operation inefficient and private firms financially weak. It addresses surplus crews, unions, shipping associations, company reorganization, and purge requirements. It proposes time charters with incentives, followed by route competition, rate adjustments, commodity subsidies, and eventual removal of emergency controls. Its appended procedures set steps and target dates.

subfiles.title: A Statement by Junsuke Itaya, President
subfiles.about: Advocates a smaller temporary shipping control agency and a larger operating role for shipowners.
subfiles.summary: Itaya argues that private operation would improve efficiency and reduce subsidies. He proposes time charters, retained central controls, revised freight rates, and stages of owner responsibility.

subfiles.title: Cover sheet for Mariners Law
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Identifies the Mariners Law as enclosure four to despatch 593.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet identifying the following copy of the Mariners Law.

subfiles.title: Mariners Law
subfiles.about: Sets definitions, masters’ duties, shipboard discipline, and the opening rule on employment contracts.
subfiles.summary: The opening chapters define mariners and shipowners’ obligations, specify masters’ navigational and rescue duties, and regulate discipline and responses to danger aboard ship. Article 31 invalidates contract terms below the law’s standards. The law continues beyond this section.
